bet.text: Keep the center of gravity low, with an extremely low chassis, so a robot geared for acceleration does not tip.

cycle.text: Coral enters the funnel and goes into a dual end effector, where two beam breaks place it the same way every time. The elevator places it on L2 to L4. The same end effector takes algae. Vision readings too far from odometry are ignored.

endgame.text: The driver drives into the cage and presses nothing. Triggers on the climber start the climb: hooks pull in, wheels turn to grab the cage, and it pulls down.

fallback.text: Redundancy is part of every design step: sensors on both sides of the climber, two beam breaks, encoders besides motor positions, three Limelights, and motor current that shows when algae is held.

gave_up.text: L3 swerve gearing puts acceleration ahead of top velocity.

changed.text: L1 was the largest change: during the season they found space in the funnel where a coral fits and can be launched with motors already wired. Metal plates became laser-cut SRPP. Printed TPU guards were added because coral could hit and break a Limelight, and a top piece keeps coral off electronics.

outcome.text: 60-6-0 in official play; ranked 6 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 112.60, Curie).
